I have been farming these 200 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I finished senior high school, so I keep a notebook and calculate my input costs against expected prices every year. But I still trust what I see with my own eyes more than anything written in a book.

My foundation is 120 mu of wheat followed by summer maize. That rotation is my secure income — wheat gives me about 550 kg per mu, and maize follows with about 650 kg. I hire the machinery service team for rotary tillage before wheat sowing in October. I use improved varieties — last year Shannong 24 yielded well, so I will sow it again. For basal fertilizer I spread one 50 kg bag of 17-20-7 compound fertilizer per mu, which gives 8.5 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphate, and 3.5 kg potash. Then I topdress twice with urea: 20 kg per mu at jointing, and another 20 kg at heading. That brings nitrogen to about 18 kg per mu. I also add a little extra potash because this field has been running low after so many years of wheat. I irrigate three times through the well — wintering water, jointing water, and grain-filling water. For pesticides, I spray insecticide twice, herbicide once after sowing, and fungicide once at heading. Four operations total.

Summer maize is Denghai 605 hybrid, sown right after wheat harvest in early June with no-tillage to save time and moisture. I put 40 kg per mu of 28-6-6 compound at sowing, which is 11 kg nitrogen, 2.5 kg phosphate, 2.5 kg potash. At the big trumpet stage, I topdress 15 kg urea per mu, bringing nitrogen to 14 kg. I irrigate twice: at tasseling and grain filling. Insecticide twice and herbicide once — three sprayings total.

I keep 40 mu for millet on the east side where the well pump pressure is weaker. Millet needs less water and fertilizer, so it suits that land. I rotary till in late April and sow an improved yellow millet variety. Basal fertilizer is 30 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound — 4.5 kg each of N, P, and K. I irrigate once at booting. Herbicide twice and insecticide once, three sprayings total. I expect 350 kg per mu.

The other 40 mu goes to squash — I grow an improved贝贝南瓜 variety. Squash brings a better price per mu when the market is good, but it is heavy on potash. I rotary till in April, apply 40 kg per mu of 18-18-18 compound as basal, then topdress urea twice at 10 kg per mu during flowering and fruit set. Total is 16 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphate, 10 kg potash per mu. I irrigate three times: at planting, flowering, and fruit expansion. Insecticide twice and fungicide once — three sprayings. Expected yield is 1200 kg per mu.

I figure this budget carefully because with 200 mu, every 10 yuan per mu is 2000 yuan. Fertilizer prices have been high, so I watch my spending. But I would rather apply a bit too much than risk a yield drop — a bad harvest on this scale is a real disaster. I also watch my neighbors with similar-sized farms, and most of them use similar rates. That gives me confidence I am not far off.
